title: The Quiet Tenant

stages.label: STOP BEING A STRANGER
stages.objective: Finch keeps the snug behind the partition after ten. Nobody joins the Skyrunners. Stand in front of him until you have stopped being a stranger.
stages.log: Finch did not sign anything and did not ask me to. He said I had stopped being a stranger, and that a tenant is somebody who pays for a roof he does not own.

stages.label: PUT YOUR HANDS IN TWO PURSES
stages.objective: The first lesson is the cheapest one. Two purses in this room, and come back whether you got them or not.
stages.log: Two purses. Finch wanted to know which hand I used and whether I had watched their eyes first. I had not.

stages.label: CRACK A GUEST'S BOX
stages.objective: Up the stair there are four rooms and four boxes at four bed-feet. One of them is not yours. Open it.
stages.log: Cracked a box above the stair. Finch says a box is easier than a purse and worth three of one, and that this is why the trade eats people.

stages.label: GET ON THE ROOF
stages.objective: You have been walking past the way up all week. Stand against an outside wall on the guest floor and take the lead over the taproom.
stages.log: Stood on the roof of the Gilded Gull. Nobody looked up. Finch says nobody ever does, and that this is the whole of the guild's secret.

stages.label: CROSS TO THE NEXT ROOF
stages.objective: A roof on its own is a trap. Line the alley up and go over it. The lead runs west from the Gull with two tiles of air in the way.
stages.log: Crossed the alley west of the Gull. Finch calls the roofs a road and the street a room, and he is not being clever about it.

stages.label: SELL WHAT YOU TOOK
stages.objective: Coin is coin and everything else is a thing. A thing has to be sold to somebody, and the somebody is Finch.
stages.log: Sold Finch what I had taken. He paid a share of what it is worth and told me the share goes up with the rung, which is the only honest wage the roofs pay.

stages.label: LEAN ON SOMEBODY
stages.objective: The cheapest coin in the ward is the coin somebody hands you. It costs nothing but what people think of you, and you have been spending that anyway.
stages.log: Leaned on somebody in the taproom. It worked because of what the ward has heard about me and not because of anything I said, which Finch says is the lesson.

stages.label: RUN A BALE PAST THE WATCH
stages.objective: There is a bale in the snug. Take it out of the door. Watchman Cull drinks by the threshold after nine and he has a memory for cargo.
stages.log: Carried the bale out past Cull. Finch paid without counting it, which he says is the difference between a wage and a share.

stages.label: ASK WHAT A TENANT IS
stages.objective: You have done every one of the things this ward calls crime. Ask Finch what comes after them.
stages.log: Finch says there is nothing after them. There is only doing them for somebody, and that the roofs will start asking. He says the word for what I am is tenant, and that it means the same on a roof as it does in a ledger: I pay for something I will never own.

notes: S5 addition. content/raws/quests/quests.json is the owner's authored canon and is UNTOUCHED; content/raws/quests/flame_disciple.json is S4's and is untouched too. This is a THIRD stages-shaped file in the same directory and it loads for its shape, not its name. WHO: `finch` is the owner's own notable -- content/raws/names/notables.json, 'Finch, the quiet tenant', sited at LAIR_SKYRUNNER -- and content/raws/factions/ranks.json's own note already says the Skyrunners' first rung is called Tenant BECAUSE of that epithet. The line is named for it. WHAT IT TEACHES: every criminal act this build actually simulates, in the order a person would learn them -- a purse, a box, the way up, the way across, the fence, the lean, and a bale carried past the law -- so that a player who finishes it has done each one once and knows where each one lives. THE VOCABULARY: `oath` and `talk` are S4's; `tally` is S5's and is `alms` with its counter named rather than assumed, which is why the Mission's line needed no edit. Every counter string here is one the crime vocabulary itself produces (sim/crime.cpp, crimeTally) or one the body produces (climbs, leaps) -- a stage counting something nothing ever counts would be a stage that cannot be finished, and that is the one thing this schema exists to prevent. NO STAGE IS GATED BY A ROLL, per DECISIONS.md's S3 ruling. CANON: DOCKS-GAZETTEER section 2.5 (rooftops are unseemly for every Trojian except a presented Wielder, which is why the poor live there and why burglars use the rooftop-slum layer as a highway) and section 3.1 K35 (the Skyrunner's Roost is unmarked and must never appear on a discoverable list -- nothing here names or maps it). Finch's own authored micro-history with Gullet Mag (gossip.finch-mag-loyalty) is left where it is and not retold.
